title: Two Left
description: Lillith buys another life at 2 AM. The coil is honest. Each chorus has one fewer ding; the last chorus has none and she still holds out her hand.
stylePrompt: Vending-machine Motown / girl-group soul, 108 BPM, F-sharp minor. Dry close female lead (Lillith, bright, transactional, no belt). Three deadpan backing singers who only sing inventory counts — "three," "two," "one" — never "love," never "baby." Kick is a coin slot. Snare is a coil-release thunk. Tambourine on the ands. Baritone sax that plays the vending-motor hum as a riff. No strings. No key change. **Structural flaw:** a sampled coil-drop ding after every chorus, counting down remaining stock. Intro has three dings. After chorus 1, two. After chorus 2, one. After the final chorus, silence where the ding belongs; she still holds the last note as if the heart is coming. Do not add a fake ding in the outro to be kind. Mood: 2 AM sidewalk, one streetlamp, a machine that is better at accounting than anyone she knows. Runtime ~1:40–2:00. Do not use Rubella (she already has a dying device). Do not use Continuity Voice.
lyrics:
[Intro — three dings, then the slot]
(ding)
(ding)
(ding)
Two left after this.
I know. I counted.

[Verse 1]
I did not come here to discuss it
I came here with a fish
The slot takes what the slot takes
The coil does not negotiate
You can see the hearts from the sidewalk
You can see how many are not there

[Pre-Chorus]
I am not asking for nine
I am asking for the one that drops
I have been this person before
I have the receipt in my mouth

[Chorus]
Two left
Two left after this
I pay, it drops, I leave
Nobody has to watch
Two left
That is still a number
That is still enough to be rude about
(ding)
(ding)

[Verse 2]
The dog on the corner has a newspaper
He is not the clerk
He is not the choir
He is the only one here with an opinion
I do not owe him a thank you
The machine does not either

[Pre-Chorus]
One of these is for later
One of these is for the thing I already did
I am restocking. That is all.
Do not make it a lesson

[Chorus 2]
Two left
Then one left
I pay, it drops, I leave
The tray is cold on purpose
Two left
I will be back when I am back
The coil will still be honest
(ding)

[Bridge — sax motor-hum only]
I have used more than I am admitting
The empty coil is not a metaphor
It is an empty coil
I can see the next heart from here
I am not taking it. I said two.
I am keeping my word to a machine
Which is more than I do for a room

[Final Chorus — no ding]
Two left
Then none that I am allowed
I pay, it drops, I leave
I hold out my hand
Two left
(silence where the ding belongs)
I am still holding it.
I know.
I counted.
notes:
## What the song is
Lillith at a vending machine that sells lives. She is restocking, not praying. The cat from the cartoon parking lot (`life-vending`) is the usual customer; tonight she is doing the errand herself and does not want a witness. The dog with the newspaper can judge. The machine cannot. That is why she likes it.

The joke is inventory. Nobody says "nine lives." Nobody thanks the coil.
